blocks.c: I showed it the front of the book.

I held it up in the beam of my own torch in a warehouse under a building, and I turned the pages slowly, and I read them out loud, because I did not know whether it could see and I was not going to make an assumption that cost me a face.

OUTSTANDING. Item one: how I take my coffee. Noted the 16th. Item two: the name of my street. Noted the 16th. Item three: the thing I used to hum. Noted the 16th, amended the 17th to add that it was four notes and went down at the end.
"That amendment is dated after the surrender," said the voice.
"It's dated after the discovery. There's no rule that says I have to notice on the same day. Show me where it says that."
"...We would have to consult the schedule."
"Then consult it," I said. "I'll wait. I'm on shift until six."
Something happened in the dark that I can only describe as a room full of paper being extremely annoyed.

Then, from about forty feet away, at the end of the rack, a light came on: a single fluorescent tube, flickering the way ours does in November, over a desk that had not been there thirty seconds earlier.

There was a chair at the desk. There was a woman sitting in the chair with her hands flat on the table in front of her, and she was in a navy polo shirt with a yellow logo, and she looked up at me and her face was absolutely furious.
"Oduya," said Wen Aguilar, "what did I say about arguing with it before you've read clause fourteen?"
